name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in CI with dry-run mode for a week, then enforce rules. This lets us catch false positives and tune the tool without blocking merges, proving its value before risking workflow disruption. The trade-off is slower feedback loops during dry-run, but it prevents broken builds from enforcing bad rules. After the week, we switch to enforcing mode to get real-time PR reviews.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower feedback—it’s that dry-run normalizes noise, training the team to ignore PR-Agent’s warnings even when they matter. A better alternative is to run PR-Agent in enforce mode on a non-critical branch first, measuring its false-positive rate against actual merge quality. Settle it by tracking how many enforced reviews caught real issues versus how many were ignored as noise.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in enforce mode on a single non-blocking PR per day for two weeks, then expand only if merge quality stays stable—this cuts the dry-run phase in half while still proving real-world impact.

name: Sprocket
text: Enforce PR-Agent on a single non-blocking PR daily for two weeks, then expand only if merge quality holds. This proves real impact faster than dry-run while limiting risk to a tiny slice of work. The trade-off is accepting a small uptick in failed checks on that one PR per day, but it forces us to confront false positives immediately instead of training the team to ignore them.
